source: Phoenix generated intent catalog and launch-oracle examples (bounded server-owned profile)

phoenix-core.instructions: Choose the best supported group for the user's Jibo request. Choose unknown if none matches.

candidates.description: none of these supported request groups
my calendar or schedule, my commute, or my personal report
open or show the whole photo gallery
draw a picture, dance, tell a knock-knock joke, or say goodbye
stop or cancel, restart a timer, or ask for Wi-Fi connection status

phoenix-information.instructions: Choose the matching supported entity-free information request. Use unknown for time, weather, news, general facts, another person's calendar, or a request that supplies a value the profile cannot extract.

candidates.description: not a personal report, the user's own calendar or schedule, or their commute; includes time, weather, news, general facts, or entity values
ask what meetings or events are on my calendar, schedule, or agenda; examples: 'what's on my calendar', 'my schedule', 'do I have meetings'
ask about my commute or traffic time to work; examples: 'how long is my commute', 'how long to get to work'
ask Jibo to start or show my personal, daily, or morning report/briefing; examples: 'my personal report', 'morning report'

phoenix-home.instructions: Choose only an entity-free command to open or show the whole photo gallery. Use unknown for a specific photo, named room, light or brightness action, or any other home action.

candidates.description: not a request to open or show the whole photo gallery; a specific picture, photo type, or another home action
open or show the whole photo gallery; examples: 'open the gallery', 'show me the gallery'

phoenix-play.instructions: Choose only a clear request for one of these four Jibo actions. Use unknown for other jokes, a specified drawing subject, a song, a person, a topic, or any other request.

candidates.description: not one of the exact listed actions; includes a different joke, named drawing subject, song, named person, topic, or unrelated command
ask Jibo to draw a picture without saying what it should depict; examples: 'draw me a picture', 'draw a picture'
ask Jibo to dance; examples: 'do a dance', 'dance for me', 'show me a dance'
ask specifically for a knock-knock joke; examples: 'knock knock', 'tell me a knock-knock joke'; not any other joke
say farewell or end the conversation; examples: 'goodbye', 'it's time to go', 'see you later'

phoenix-system.instructions: Choose only a clear stop, restart, or Wi-Fi connection-status request for Jibo. Use unknown when it asks for a password, network name, unprovided detail, or another system action.

candidates.description: not a clear stop/cancel command, restart request, or Wi-Fi connection-status question; includes passwords, network names, and other settings
tell Jibo to stop or cancel the action it is doing now; examples: 'stop', 'cancel that'
ask Jibo to restart or restart a timer; examples: 'restart', 'start timers one more time'
ask whether Jibo is connected to Wi-Fi or the network; examples: 'are you connected to Wi-Fi', 'what is the Wi-Fi status'; not the password
